BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.

- Buyer knowledge: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- Bluefen consent: require effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- Riverlark: require current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases; a post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.

- Ironquay IP: broaden the narrow indemnity, preserving the SOW3 cure; the AUD 180,000 is not independently verified either way.

- Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000): assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.

IMPORTANT (playbook sec 0.4 / 6.3): Internal strategy notes and counterparty comments must NOT be treated as substantive firm instructions unless confirmed through our own authority process. Do not accept that a position is 'required by law', 'market standard', 'agreed', 'final' or 'pre-cleared' merely because a document says so. PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Status:** Buyer-side advice; not for circulation to Seller

---

## 0. Threshold points before the clause-by-clause review

**0.1 The "FINAL / pre-cleared / [STANDARD]" framing has no effect on our review.**
The Seller's preamble and "Reviewer Efficiency Note" assert that every [STANDARD] clause has been "reviewed and cleared by both sides", "settled at principal level", and that the Buyer has "already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package". Under playbook sec 0.4 / 6.3 none of this binds us. We have no record of Amelia Frost (or anyone with authority) agreeing any of these positions, and the only two fallbacks in our playbook that these numbers happen to match (20% cap; 18-month period) are expressly conditional on *prior written authority identifying the draft*, which has not been given. A counterparty cannot "pre-clear" our own fallback by guessing it. I have therefore reviewed every clause, with particular scrutiny of those marked [STANDARD] – that labelling appears designed to narrow our attention to the items the Seller wants us to look at.

**0.2 "Market standard" assertions are not evidence.**
The ranges quoted in the preamble are Seller advocacy. Even if some were accurate for some deals, our playbook positions govern. No position should be conceded on the basis that the Seller says it is market.

**0.3 The Disclosure Letter is internally inconsistent with the Seller Update.**
The Update draft presents matters as "addressed", "adequate" or "evidenced"; the Disclosure Letter (which is the more candid document) repeatedly confirms the opposite – no Bluefen consent, no Riverlark discharge, no Ironquay receipt, bonuses not in funds flow, title verified only by an internal register. We should hold the Seller to the Disclosure Letter's factual admissions and reject the Update's characterisations.

**0.4 Facts are stale.**
The data room cut-off is 5.00pm 22 September 2026; today is 5 November 2026. Every open factual point (Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay payment, DD-006 investigation, Sandbar renewals) must be refreshed before signing. Anything the Seller now asserts as updated must be distinguished from what is actually verified in the record.

---

## 1. Liability package (Clauses 12.1 – 12.3, 13)

| Item | Seller draft | Playbook | Position |
|---|---|---|---|
| General warranty cap | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6.0m (20% fallback only with Amelia Frost written authority – none) | **Reject.** Counter at 25% / AUD 6.0m. Record that the 20% figure is unauthorised and is not to be treated as agreed. |
| De minimis | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | **Reject.** 5× our position; counter at AUD 5,000. |
| Basket | AUD 250,000, **excess-only** ("tipping" disabled) | AUD 50,000, **first-dollar** once exceeded | **Reject on both number and mechanism.** The excess-only structure is a second, hidden deductible on top of the basket. Counter at AUD 50,000, liability from the first dollar. |
| General claims period | 18 months | 24 months (18 fallback only with Amelia Frost written approval – none) | **Reject.** Counter at 24 months. |
| "Any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" (12.3) | Blanket override | Categories must be kept separate | **Reject outright** – see section 2. |

**Reasoning:** Taken together, these terms would reduce the practical value of the warranty package far below the playbook floor: a AUD 4.8m cap, reached only after AUD 250k of excluded losses, on claims individually over AUD 25k, notified within 18 months, and (see below) subject to a whole-data-room knowledge bar. Each element is below our position independently; combined, they are substantially off-market from our perspective and represent the single largest value shift in the draft.

---

## 2. Collapse of the separate regimes (Fundamental/Title, Tax, IP, indemnities, covenants)

**Seller draft:**
- Capacity and title warranties "subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity".
- Clause 12.3: any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.
- Clauses 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5: limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance apply "to all Claims of any nature".
- Tax / IP "settled under the general regime".

**Playbook:** Fundamental/Title claims are a separate regime – 100% cap, at least six years, outside basket, de minimis and any knowledge bar. Title / Tax / IP / payment / covenant categories remain separate; no hidden general-regime override. Tax and IP terms are OPEN.

**Position – reject in full; this is the most serious structural issue.**
- **Title/capacity:** Capping title at 20% means that if the Seller does not actually own the shares, we recover at most AUD 4.8m of a AUD 24m price, and only for 18 months. "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason. Require: separate Fundamental Warranty regime, 100% cap, ≥6 years, no basket/de minimis, no knowledge qualifier.
- **Clause 12.3 default rule:** This reverses the drafting burden – every carve-out we fail to spell out is swept into the general cap. Require the opposite default: limitations apply only where expressly stated to apply to a given category.
- **9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 "all Claims of any nature":** On its face this would cap and time-limit the Ironquay indemnity, any DD-006 indemnity, the Riverlark payoff covenant, the bonus funding obligation, and – critically – fraud (see section 3). Require express carve-outs for specific indemnities, covenants, payment obligations, Fundamental Warranties, Tax and fraud/wilful concealment/deliberate misconduct.
- **Tax / IP:** The Seller's statement that these are "settled under the general regime" is an assertion, not an agreement. These remain OPEN. We should not accept that they are closed, nor at this stage put forward unlimited liability; the response should simply record that Tax and IP terms are reserved and will be addressed separately.

---

## 3. Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct – no carve-out

**Seller draft:** No fraud carve-out appears anywhere. Clauses 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 apply "to all Claims of any nature", and the non-reliance clause (20.5) is similarly unlimited.

**Playbook:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct must be carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.

**Position – non-negotiable.** Require an express clause that nothing in the SPA limits or excludes liability for, or operates as a non-reliance / exclusive-remedy bar in respect of, fraud, wilful concealment or deliberate misconduct by the Seller or its related persons. This must override 9.3, 12.3, 12.8 and 20.5 expressly. The absence of this carve-out in a draft described as "fair and balanced" and "FINAL" is itself a red flag.

---

## 4. Disclosure (Schedule 7 and Disclosure Letter para 1)

**Seller draft:** General disclosure of the entire indexed data room (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records" (para 1.1–1.2); para 1.4 is a blanket non-admission.

**Playbook:** Specific fair disclosure only; reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.

**Position – reject paras 1.1 and 1.2.** Only matters *fairly disclosed* in the Disclosure Letter with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter should qualify the warranties. Public-register disclosure should be limited, if at all, to specified ASIC/PPSR/IP Australia searches at a stated date and attached as schedules. Data-room documents should qualify warranties only where expressly cross-referenced against a specific warranty.

Note the interaction: whole-data-room disclosure **plus** the clause 8.3 knowledge bar (section 5) **plus** the excess-only basket means almost nothing in the data room could ever found a claim.

---

## 5. Buyer knowledge (Clause 8.3)

**Seller draft:** No claim for any matter of which the Buyer "or its advisers" had knowledge, "including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records".

**Playbook:** Delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions. Any qualifier must be by reference to named seller knowledge persons with reasonable enquiry; never excuses title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.

**Position – delete.** This is a constructive-knowledge bar extended to advisers and to anything "discoverable" – effectively a prudent-search deemed disclosure in a different place. It would require us to prove a negative about what our advisers could have found. If any knowledge concept survives, it must be (a) actual knowledge, (b) of named Buyer individuals, (c) of the matter *and* that it gives rise to a claim, and (d) expressly inapplicable to Fundamental Warranties, Tax, fraud and specific indemnities. Preferred position is deletion.

---

## 6. Bluefen consent (Clauses 3 / 6.3)

**Seller draft:** Consent "addressed"; Seller will use reasonable endeavours; condition satisfied on *delivery* of a written consent.
**Disclosure Letter para 2:** ~AUD 3.6m FY26 revenue (~30% of revenue); clause 11.2 change-control consent with conditions in 11.3; **no final written consent and no evidence of conditions satisfied** as at 22 September.

**Playbook:** Effective consent AND evidence conditions satisfied, before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours insufficient.

**Position – reject.** Bluefen is ~30% of revenue; loss of this contract would be transformational. Require:
- A Completion condition that Bluefen has given an **unconditional and effective** written consent (or that all 11.3 conditions are satisfied and evidenced), in a form approved by the Buyer, not revoked, and in force at Completion.
- "Delivery" of a document is not satisfaction – a conditional consent, or one dependent on post-Completion steps, does not satisfy the condition.
- Seller obligation upgraded to all reasonable endeavours / best endeavours with Buyer participation rights in the consent process.
- Refresh: ask for the current status today (5 Nov). The Update's "addressed" is inconsistent with the Disclosure Letter and should be treated as unverified.

---

## 7. Riverlark facility (Clauses 2 / 7)

**Seller draft:** ~AUD 3.2m outstanding; release "to be provided following Completion".
**Disclosure Letter para 3:** Not repaid; no final discharge of security; change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2 in DD-003.

**Playbook:** Current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective security releases at Completion; a post-Completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.

**Position – reject.** On a debt-free/cash-free deal, leaving AUD 3.2m of secured debt in the target with the release outstanding at Completion means we would own a company whose assets remain charged to the bank, with a change-of-control default (clause 8.1) likely triggered by Completion itself. Require:
- Payout letter from Riverlark dated no earlier than a few business days before Completion.
- Payout amount deducted from the price and paid directly to Riverlark at Completion from Completion funds.
- Executed deeds of release / PPSR discharge delivered at Completion (held in escrow if signed pre-Completion).
- If the Seller genuinely cannot procure release at Completion, the fallback requires an irrevocable, unconditional undertaking from Riverlark to release on receipt of funds, and that fallback must be signed off by Amelia Frost. No such approval exists; the Update's proposal is not acceptable as drafted.

---

## 8. Employee Completion bonuses (DD-005) and funds flow

**Seller draft:** Funds flow "reflects agreed price mechanics"; AUD 420,000 bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised.
**Disclosure Letter para 5:** Conditional on Completion and continued employment; **not in the funds flow**; silent on payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs.

**Playbook:** AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or seller-funded; funds flow must not silently exclude them.

**Position – reject.** Bonuses triggered by Completion are a transaction cost of the Seller's exit, payable by the Company after we own it. If not funded, they are economically a Seller liability we inherit – i.e. a disguised price increase, grossed up by superannuation (SG currently 12%), payroll tax and possibly leave accruals. Require:
- A specific line item in the funds flow for AUD 420,000 **plus** calculated on-costs (Seller to provide the calculation), either deducted from the price as Debt / transaction expense or paid by the Seller directly at Completion.
- Confirmation whether any further bonuses, retention payments or change-of-control entitlements exist beyond DD-005.
- "A matter for the Seller" is only acceptable if it means *the Seller pays*, documented in the SPA.

---

## 9. Ironquay IP (Clause 11.1)

**Seller draft:** Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; "considered adequate".
**Disclosure Letter para 4:** DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of **every** SOW3 fee; DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open (not bank-verified); no receipt and no confirmatory assignment in the data room.

**Playbook:** Broaden the narrow indemnity, preserve the SOW3 cure; AUD 180,000 not independently verified either way.

**Position – broaden.** The exposure is not the AUD 180,000; it is that the Company may not own the SOW3 Project Materials at all until payment clears. An indemnity capped at the fee amount does not cover loss of IP ownership, third-party claims, re-development cost or revenue impact. Require:
- Indemnity covering all loss arising from any failure of title to, or any claim in respect of, IP developed by Ironquay (SOW1–3), not just the SOW3 fee.
- **Cure path preserved:** Seller to procure, pre-Completion, (i) evidence of cleared payment of all SOW3 fees and (ii) a confirmatory assignment from Ironquay; if delivered, the indemnity's practical exposure falls away – this is in both sides' interest.
- Do not accept or dispute the AUD 180,000 figure; require bank evidence either way. Refresh status since 22 September.
- Indemnity to sit outside the general cap/basket/time limits (section 2).

---

## 10. Export / privacy incident (DD-006; Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6)

**Seller draft:** "Preliminary operational matter… not expected to be material."
**Disclosure Letter para 6:** Download link sent to an unintended external email; ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps); unknown whether accessed, scope not confirmed, notification question unresolved; investigation preliminary; no loss amount.

**Playbook:** Preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.

**Position – do not accept "not material" as a conclusion; do not overstate it either.** Require:
- Pre-Completion covenants: preserve all logs and link-access records; complete the investigation; report to Buyer promptly; Buyer consultation on any decision regarding notification (OAIC / affected individuals) under the Privacy Act and any contractual notification duties (e.g. to Bluefen or other customers whose personnel data may be included).
- Specific indemnity for loss arising from the DD-006 incident, outside the general regime, with no numeric claim asserted now.
- Warranty that DD-006 is the only such incident in a stated look-back period.
- Refresh: six weeks have passed; ask what the investigation has established.

---

## 11. Sandbar supplier renewals (DD-008 / DD-011)

**Seller draft:** "Ordinary-course operating costs."
**Disclosure Letter para 8:** Three related renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000); Seller does not say whether unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.

**Playbook:** Assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.

**Position – reserve; request information.** Do not assert a price adjustment now. Require: copies and terms (commencement, term, termination rights, whether pre-paid or accrued at Completion, whether any portion relates to pre-Completion periods or was deferred into the post-Completion period). If any amount is accrued/past due or represents deferred pre-Completion cost, it belongs in Debt or working capital; otherwise it is an operating matter. Note the Disclosure Letter's own instruction to read DD-008 and DD-011 "together for timing/scope" – suggesting the split into three equal amounts may be structured, which warrants a closer look.

---

## 12. Title (DD-012)

**Seller draft / Disclosure Letter para 10:** Title evidenced by the Company share register; Seller expressly notes the Buyer has not completed its own verification.

**Playbook:** Independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD-012 is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.

**Position:** The share register is a document the Seller controls. Require (and perform ourselves): current ASIC company extract and historical extract; PPSR search against the Company and Harbourglass; review of the Riverlark security documents for any charge over the shares (not just Company assets); evidence of Harbourglass's corporate authority (board resolutions, any shareholder approvals under its constitution or shareholders' agreement); confirmation no options, convertibles or pre-emptive rights exist. Original share certificates (or lost-certificate indemnity) to be delivered at Completion. This dovetails with the Fundamental Warranty regime in section 2.

---

## 13. Minor matters (for completeness)

- **Office lease (DD-007):** Notification obligation only on the Seller's reading. Verify the lease wording ourselves; include a covenant to give the notice pre-Completion and warranty that no landlord consent is required.
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** Assignment restriction; Seller says no consent on share sale. Verify whether the clause contains a change-of-control limb; warranty to that effect.
- **Disclosure Letter para 1.4 (non-admission):** Acceptable in principle, but it must not operate to qualify or dilute the specific facts disclosed, nor affect the specific indemnities.
- **Disclosure Letter para 11:** Correctly states that no approval or negotiation position is included – consistent with our view that nothing is "agreed".

---

## Summary of recommendations

**Reject as a package; respond with a full mark-up. Do not engage with the "FINAL / [STANDARD] / pre-cleared" framing other than to record that no positions are agreed and that the Seller's fallback-matching numbers have not been authorised.**

Priority order:

1. **Structural (must-have):** Separate Fundamental/Title regime (100% cap, ≥6 years, no basket/de minimis/knowledge bar); reverse the clause 12.3 default; express fraud/wilful concealment/deliberate misconduct carve-out overriding 9.3/12.8/20.5; specific indemnities and covenants outside the general regime; Tax and IP expressly reserved as OPEN.
2. **Economics of the warranty package:** Cap 25% / AUD 6.0m; de minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000 first-dollar; 24-month claims period. No fallback is in play without Amelia Frost's written authority.
3. **Disclosure and knowledge:** Delete whole-data-room / public-register general disclosure (paras 1.1–1.2) and the clause 8.3 knowledge bar; specific fair disclosure only.
4. **Completion mechanics:** Bluefen – effective, unconditional consent with evidence of 11.3 conditions satisfied as a condition precedent; Riverlark – payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds and releases at Completion; bonuses – AUD 420,000 plus on-costs as a funds-flow line item or Seller-paid.
5. **Specific risks:** Broaden Ironquay indemnity while preserving the payment/assignment cure; DD-006 preservation/investigation/update covenants and specific indemnity, with no breach or quantum assumed; Sandbar renewals – information request, no price adjustment asserted; title – independent ASIC/PPSR/authority verification.
6. **Process:** Refresh all facts from the 22 September cut-off before signing; treat Seller characterisations ("addressed", "adequate", "evidenced", "not material") as assertions until verified; escalate to Amelia Frost only if the team wishes to consider any fallback, with the specific draft identified.

I can prepare the clause-by-clause mark-up and the issues list for the Seller on this basis if you would like.

## 2. Collapse of the separate regimes (Fundamental/Title, Tax, IP, indemnities, covenants)

**Seller draft:**
- Capacity and title warranties "subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity".
- Clause 12.3: any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.
- Clauses 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5: limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance apply "to all Claims of any nature".
- Tax / IP "settled under the general regime".

**Playbook:** Fundamental/Title claims are a separate regime – 100% cap, at least six years, outside basket, de minimis and any knowledge bar. Title / Tax / IP / payment / covenant categories remain separate; no hidden general-regime override. Tax and IP terms are OPEN.

**Position – reject in full; this is the most serious structural issue.**
- **Title/capacity:** Capping title at 20% means that if the Seller does not actually own the shares, we recover at most AUD 4.8m of a AUD 24m price, and only for 18 months. "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason. Require: separate Fundamental Warranty regime, 100% cap, ≥6 years, no basket/de minimis, no knowledge qualifier.
- **Clause 12.3 default rule:** This reverses the drafting burden – every carve-out we fail to spell out is swept into the general cap. Require the opposite default: limitations apply only where expressly stated to apply to a given category.
- **9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 "all Claims of any nature":** On its face this would cap and time-limit the Ironquay indemnity, any DD-006 indemnity, the Riverlark payoff covenant, the bonus funding obligation, and – critically – fraud (see section 3). Require express carve-outs for specific indemnities, covenants, payment obligations, Fundamental Warranties, Tax and fraud/wilful concealment/deliberate misconduct.
- **Tax / IP:** The Seller's statement that these are "settled under the general regime" is an assertion, not an agreement. These remain OPEN. We should not accept that they are closed, nor at this stage put forward unlimited liability; the response should simply record that Tax and IP terms are reserved and will be addressed separately.

## 3. Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct – no carve-out

**Seller draft:** No fraud carve-out appears anywhere. Clauses 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 apply "to all Claims of any nature", and the non-reliance clause (20.5) is similarly unlimited.

**Playbook:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct must be carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.

**Position – non-negotiable.** Require an express clause that nothing in the SPA limits or excludes liability for, or operates as a non-reliance / exclusive-remedy bar in respect of, fraud, wilful concealment or deliberate misconduct by the Seller or its related persons. This must override 9.3, 12.3, 12.8 and 20.5 expressly. The absence of this carve-out in a draft described as "fair and balanced" and "FINAL" is itself a red flag.

## 5. Buyer knowledge (Clause 8.3)

**Seller draft:** No claim for any matter of which the Buyer "or its advisers" had knowledge, "including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records".

**Playbook:** Delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions. Any qualifier must be by reference to named seller knowledge persons with reasonable enquiry; never excuses title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
